mechanism_narrative: A negative change in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month indicates monetary easing, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 207.5, it signals persistent inflation that typically leads to aggressive monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 207.5, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% and decline in UNRATE below 4.0% signals a late-cycle monetary tightening with labor market strength, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and UNRATE < 4.0) fails to predict negative returns when 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (HOUST > 1300 and GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, the signal (HOUST decline) fails when 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances, or the signal's Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a deteriorating labor market that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-growth regimes (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply chain activity, which typically produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The signal (INDPRO decline) fails to predict negative returns when 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of high-growth regime instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% and employment growth (PAYEMS) slows below 0.5% monthly, it indicates a monetary tightening cycle with labor market softening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and PAYEMS growth < 0.5%) fails when 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which typically produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of the macro regime.
failure_condition: The signal (HOUST decline) fails when 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
